findings.rationale: Accepted: §2 docs bullet now pins the redesign row Status to the literal `open`.
Accepted: §4.1 now cites base-suites-d7912c7e.txt (twelve commands, all exit 0 at base, detached checkout, isolation suite under its host variable) instead of a memory note.

Accepted: §1.2 now maps launcher exit to decision exhaustively — 0+JSON line → ready; 0 without a line → rejected; 124 → rejected "probe timed out … no diagnostic"; any other exit → rejected "exit <n>: <first stderr line|no diagnostic>"; defaultCleanroomProbe takes { launcher, timeoutMs, bwrap } so the routing suite drives the real default probe with stub launchers (exit 0 / exit 2 + stderr / sleeping with timeoutMs 500); acceptance row updated.

Accepted: `unknown` removed. The default adapter always exists and the blind block runs before missionMode is computed (campaign-intake.js:1481-1483), so the decision set is ready|rejected and anything else is cleanroom_probe_adapter_invalid via the existing requireDecision rail; §1.2, §2.6, §4, §6 aligned; test case added.

Accepted as a clarity defect, mechanism unchanged: the launcher sets the seat HOME to /home/review itself (cleanroom-launch.sh:253-256) and the deny check runs inside the namespace where the operator HOME is not mounted; `--preflight --deny-path <repo> --deny-path <HOME>` already exits 0 on this host (cleanroom-launch.test.sh:178-181). §1.2 now states which HOME the child sees and why host-probe is satisfiable.

Accepted: verified at base d7912c7e that no schema encloses intake steps[] owner names, so §2 now says NONE with the evidence and explains why check-contract-schema.js stays green (advisory lands in the existing capability_warnings[] field); the max_changed_files 18 > 16 sentence now names the rail defect it works around instead of reading as an unresolved self-flag.
Accepted: the stale footnote (check-contract-schema.js "is node, fix") is replaced by the base record; the base run is in the evidence dir (base-suites-d7912c7e.txt) before sealing.
Accepted: §2 now states grok is in schemas/review-loop-contract.schema.json reviewer_runner.enum and in neither tier at base.
Accepted: the parity block reads reviewer_runner.enum from review-loop-contract.schema.json at test time (minus auto), never a hard-coded list.
Accepted: the full Context string is written out (234 bytes, under the 240 cap), Status pinned to `open`, and v2.36.63 in text is stated to be a release-commit pin owned by depth-0.
